title: Direct-XOR optimality for primitive F4 subfield multiplication
summary: Determine whether repeating an optimal proper-subfield multiplication matrix remains optimal in an extension field, beginning with the primitive F4 direct-XOR case.

formal_statement.body: Let $\alpha\in\mathbb F_4\setminus\mathbb F_2$ and represent multiplication by $\alpha$ on $\mathbb F_{2^{2d}}$ by a binary matrix $A$. Determine the minimum direct-XOR cost among matrices satisfying $A^2+A+I=0$, and compare it with the block diagonal sum of $d$ copies of the optimal $2\times2$ matrix.

scope.domain: Finite-field multiplication and linear implementation cost
parameters: Binary matrix weight and direct-XOR count
scope.unresolved_remainder: General proper subfields and the sequential-XOR metric are not covered.

provenance.note: Kölsch explicitly says Problem 6.5.4 repeats a problem mentioned in Beierle--Kranz--Leander [5]; the 2016 CRYPTO paper is therefore the earliest confirmed source and the thesis is a restatement.

citations.label: Beierle--Kranz--Leander, lightweight finite-field multiplication
citations.locator: Section 6, generalized proper-subfield multiplication problem, CRYPTO 2016, pp. 625-653

progress.summary: Beierle, Kranz, and Leander pose the proper-subfield multiplication optimality question for direct and sequential XOR cost.
Kölsch explicitly repeats the cited proper-subfield multiplication problem as Problem 6.5.4 and specializes it to the primitive F4 case.
